newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cosmonaut asks why kitchen tap sent from Earth.
newsitem.headline: Cosmonaut asks why kitchen tap sent from Earth.

text.p: The head of the Russian-American crew battling to save the Mir space station asked Mission Control on Monday why it had sent them what looked like an old kitchen tap.

"We are trying to get an answer from you what is that tap which looks like one in the kitchen. I found it in a sack. Can you tell me what it is?" Tsiblieyev said in a television exchange with Mission Control at Korolyov outside Moscow.
But no one could immediately tell him.
"Wait and we will find out," replied a Mission Control official.

Mission Control sent a stock of repair tools to Mir last week on a cargo craft. The tools are needed to carry out the complicated task of entering the Spektr module, holed in a collision with another cargo craft on June 25.
In the same television exchange 15 minutes of film were transmitted to the Mir showing Deputy Flight Commander Sergei Krikalyov undertaking a similar operation in a swimming pool.
An accompanying commentary pointed out which operations were better done by hand and which using a wrench. But there was no mention of the tap.
